lessons.title: Negotiating a Realistic Deadline
lessons.theme: 在不破坏合作关系的前提下协商交期
objectives: 解释延期原因而不推卸责任
提出带条件的替代方案
用缓和表达处理分歧
warmUpQuestions: What usually causes delays in your work?
How do you say no to an unrealistic request without sounding negative?
lessons.passage: A customer asked us to deliver the entire order by Friday. At first, the deadline seemed impossible because one component would not arrive until Thursday afternoon. Instead of simply rejecting the request, I explained the constraint and separated the order into two batches. We could ship the urgent items on Friday and send the remainder the following Tuesday. I also offered daily progress updates so the customer would not be left uncertain. The customer accepted the proposal because it protected their most important launch date. The experience reminded me that a good negotiation is not about winning an argument. It is about identifying the other side's real priority and building a workable solution around it.
lessons.passageTranslation: 客户要求我们在星期五前交付全部订单。起初这个期限似乎不可能，因为其中一种零件要到星期四下午才能到货。我没有直接拒绝，而是说明限制，并把订单分成两批。紧急产品可以周五发出，其余部分下周二发出。我还提出每天汇报进度，避免客户因信息不足而不安。客户接受了方案，因为它保障了最重要的上市日期。这次经历让我意识到，好的谈判不是赢得争论，而是找出对方真正的优先事项，并围绕它建立可行方案。

lessons.title: Reading News Critically
lessons.theme: 识别报道中的事实、观点与缺失信息
objectives: 区分事实陈述与推断
指出报道缺少的证据
用谨慎语言表达判断
warmUpQuestions: What makes you trust a news story?
Have you ever shared information that later proved inaccurate?
lessons.passage: A convincing headline can create the impression that an issue has already been settled. However, responsible readers pause before accepting the conclusion. They ask who produced the information, what evidence is available, and whether alternative explanations were considered. Numbers can also mislead without being false. For example, a report may describe a fifty-percent increase but fail to mention that the number rose from two cases to three. Images are equally powerful because they can be genuine while still being presented without context. Critical reading does not mean assuming that every source is dishonest. It means matching the strength of our conclusion to the quality of the available evidence.
lessons.passageTranslation: 一个有说服力的标题会让人觉得问题已有定论。然而，负责任的读者在接受结论前会暂停思考：信息由谁发布，有什么证据，是否考虑了其他解释。数字即使真实也可能产生误导。例如，报道说增长了百分之五十，却没说明数字只是从两例增加到三例。图片也同样有力量，因为它可能真实，却脱离了语境。批判性阅读并不是认定所有来源都不诚实，而是让结论的确定程度与现有证据的质量相匹配。

vocabulary.definition: finally decided or no longer in doubt
vocabulary.example: The debate is far from settled.

vocabulary.definition: another possible reason for the same result
vocabulary.example: The article ignored several alternative explanations.

vocabulary.definition: without the background needed for correct understanding
vocabulary.example: The quotation is misleading without context.

vocabulary.definition: make the degree of certainty appropriate to the evidence
vocabulary.example: We should match the strength of our claim to the data.

quiz.question: Why can a percentage be misleading?

quiz.explanation: The passage gives the example of an increase from two to three.

quiz.question: What does critical reading require?
quiz.explanation: The conclusion should be no stronger than the evidence supports.

lessons.title: Sustainable Choices at Work
lessons.theme: 讨论环保措施中的效果、成本与取舍
objectives: 比较环保方案的实际影响
讨论短期成本与长期收益
提出有依据的建议
warmUpQuestions: Which environmental action at work has the greatest impact?
When can a green choice create an unexpected cost?
lessons.passage: Companies often announce environmental targets, but the most visible action is not always the most effective one. Replacing plastic cups may improve public perception, yet changes in energy use, transport and product design can have a much larger impact. The difficulty is that these measures require investment and cooperation across departments. A realistic plan should therefore compare the full life cycle of each option rather than focusing on a single material. It should also measure progress in a way that employees and customers can understand. If a target is ambitious but impossible to verify, it may create more suspicion than trust. Sustainability becomes credible when an organization explains both what it has achieved and where it is still falling short.
lessons.passageTranslation: 公司经常宣布环保目标，但最显眼的行动不一定最有效。更换塑料杯可能改善公众印象，但能源使用、运输和产品设计的改变可能影响更大。困难在于这些措施需要投资和跨部门合作。因此，现实的计划应比较每个选择的完整生命周期，而不是只关注一种材料；还应以员工和客户能理解的方式衡量进展。如果目标雄心勃勃却无法验证，反而可能引起更多怀疑。一个组织既说明已取得的成果，也坦诚仍有不足，可持续发展才更可信。

vocabulary.example: The campaign improved public perception of the brand.

lessons.title: Giving Constructive Feedback
lessons.theme: 在明确问题的同时保持尊重和可执行性
objectives: 描述具体行为而非评价人格
说明影响并提出下一步
回应不同意见
warmUpQuestions: What makes feedback difficult to accept?
Do you prefer direct or indirect feedback? Why?
lessons.passage: Feedback becomes useful when it is specific enough to guide action. Saying that a presentation was weak gives the speaker little direction. Explaining that the main recommendation appeared only at the end is more helpful because the problem can be corrected. Timing also matters. Immediate feedback can prevent repeated mistakes, but a tense public discussion may cause the recipient to become defensive. A private conversation after emotions have settled is often more productive. Finally, feedback should allow room for information we may not have. Asking what influenced a decision can reveal constraints that were invisible to us. Constructive feedback combines clarity with curiosity: it states the observed impact while remaining open to another perspective.
lessons.passageTranslation: 反馈要具体到能够指导行动，才真正有用。只说演示很差，演讲者不知道如何改进；说明主要建议直到最后才出现，则更有帮助，因为问题可以修正。时机也很重要。立即反馈能防止重复错误，但在紧张的公开讨论中可能让对方产生防御。等情绪平静后私下沟通往往更有效。最后，反馈应给未知信息留出空间。询问某个决定受什么因素影响，可能揭示我们看不到的限制。建设性反馈把清晰与好奇结合起来：既说明观察到的影响，也对另一种观点保持开放。

lessons.title: The Trade-offs of Hybrid Work
lessons.theme: 用平衡论证讨论远程与办公室协作
objectives: 构建包含让步的观点
比较效率与协作成本
总结复杂讨论
warmUpQuestions: Which tasks are easier at home?
What can remote teams lose besides face-to-face contact?
lessons.passage: Hybrid work is often discussed as a choice between freedom and control, but the real issue is coordination. Employees may concentrate better at home and avoid a long commute. At the same time, spontaneous questions become scheduled meetings, and new colleagues may struggle to learn informal practices. Requiring everyone to attend the office every day solves some coordination problems but removes much of the flexibility people value. A better policy defines which activities genuinely benefit from shared space. Teams might meet in person for planning, difficult decisions and relationship-building, while protecting remote time for focused individual work. The success of such a policy depends less on the number of office days than on whether expectations are clear and applied consistently.
lessons.passageTranslation: 混合办公常被描述为自由与控制之间的选择，但真正的问题是协调。员工在家可能更专注，也免去长途通勤；与此同时，临时提问变成预约会议，新同事也可能难以学到非正式的工作方式。要求所有人每天到办公室能解决部分协调问题，却会失去大家重视的灵活性。更好的政策应明确哪些活动真正受益于共享空间。团队可在线下进行规划、困难决策和关系建设，同时保留远程时间处理需要专注的个人工作。政策是否成功，与其说取决于到办公室几天，不如说取决于期望是否清晰并得到一致执行。

lessons.title: Handling a Complex Complaint
lessons.theme: 承认影响、核实责任并恢复客户信任
objectives: 在事实未完全明确时承担沟通责任
提出调查和补救步骤
避免过度承诺
warmUpQuestions: What does an angry customer need first: facts, empathy or compensation?
Why can an immediate promise create a second problem?
lessons.passage: When a complaint is complex, the first response should not attempt to solve everything. Its purpose is to show that the problem has been understood and that a reliable process has begun. A useful response acknowledges the customer's experience, summarizes the issue and confirms when the next update will arrive. It should distinguish between what is already known and what still needs investigation. This prevents the company from making a promise it may later have to withdraw. Compensation may be appropriate, but offering it before understanding the cause can distract from the customer's real concern. Trust is usually restored through accurate updates and completed actions rather than through an impressive first message.
lessons.passageTranslation: 当投诉很复杂时，第一次回复不应试图解决所有问题，而应表明问题已被理解，并且可靠的处理流程已经启动。有效的回复会承认客户的经历，概括问题，并确认下次更新的时间；还应区分已知事实和仍需调查的内容，避免公司作出之后不得不撤回的承诺。赔偿可能合适，但在了解原因前提出赔偿，可能偏离客户真正关心的问题。恢复信任通常依靠准确的更新和落实的行动，而不是一封看起来很漂亮的首次回复。

lessons.title: Weekly Integration Challenge
lessons.theme: 整合本周语言：分析、协商、反馈与总结
objectives: 整合本周高频表达
连续表达观点两分钟
根据证据修正自己的结论
warmUpQuestions: Which lesson changed how you would communicate at work?
Which task was hardest: understanding, speaking or writing?
lessons.passage: Progress at B2 level is rarely about learning one more grammar rule. It is increasingly about control: choosing language that fits the purpose, recognizing uncertainty and connecting ideas clearly. A strong learner can explain a position, acknowledge a reasonable objection and still make a practical recommendation. This week’s topics may appear different, yet they share one skill. Whether we evaluate a headline, negotiate a deadline or answer a complaint, we must separate facts from assumptions and make our reasoning visible. Fluency matters, but reliable communication also requires revision. Recording an answer, noticing where the argument becomes vague and trying again is not a sign of failure. It is the process through which confident language becomes precise language.
lessons.passageTranslation: 到了 B2 水平，进步很少只是再学一条语法规则，而越来越在于控制力：选择符合目的的语言、识别不确定性并清晰连接观点。优秀的学习者能够解释立场，承认合理反对意见，同时仍提出可执行建议。本周主题看似不同，却共享一种能力：无论评估标题、协商期限还是回复投诉，我们都必须区分事实与假设，并让推理过程清晰可见。流利很重要，但可靠沟通也需要修订。录下回答、发现论证含糊之处再尝试一次，并不是失败，而是让自信表达变得精准的过程。

vocabulary.example: B2 learners need greater control, not just more vocabulary.

lessons.title: Clarifying a Change Request
lessons.theme: 在项目进行中澄清客户的新要求
objectives: 确认需求变化的具体范围
解释变化对时间和成本的影响
提出清晰的下一步安排
warmUpQuestions: What information do you need before accepting a change request?
How can you discuss extra cost without sounding unhelpful?
lessons.passage: Halfway through a packaging project, the customer asked us to replace the original material and add two new tests. The request sounded simple, but it affected several parts of the schedule. Before agreeing, I asked whether the new material was required for every model and which test standard the customer expected. I then summarized the change in writing and explained its likely impact on cost, sample approval and delivery. Rather than saying that the request was impossible, I offered two routes. We could keep the original launch date by changing only the priority models, or apply the change to the full order and move delivery by one week. The customer chose the first option. Clear questions prevented us from making an expensive assumption and gave both sides a shared basis for the decision.
lessons.passageTranslation: 包装项目进行到一半时，客户要求更换原材料并增加两项测试。这个要求听起来简单，却会影响进度的多个环节。在答应之前，我先确认新材料是否适用于所有型号，以及客户要求哪一种测试标准。随后我用书面方式总结变更，并说明它可能对成本、样品批准和交付造成的影响。我没有直接说要求无法实现，而是提供两条路径：如果只更改优先型号，可以保留原上市日期；如果整批订单都变更，交付则需要延后一周。客户选择了第一种。清晰的问题避免了代价高昂的假设，也为双方决策建立了共同依据。

lessons.title: Resolving a Hotel Booking Problem
lessons.theme: 在酒店预订出现问题时清楚说明并协商解决
objectives: 有条理地说明预订问题
礼貌但坚定地提出合理要求
确认解决方案的具体细节
warmUpQuestions: What booking details should you keep before a trip?
When does a polite complaint need to become more direct?
lessons.passage: When I arrived at the hotel, the receptionist could not find my reservation, even though I had a confirmation email. The hotel was almost full, and the only available room was more expensive than the one I had booked. I remained calm and showed the booking number, dates and payment record. I explained that I understood mistakes could happen, but I should not have to pay extra for a problem I had not caused. The receptionist checked with the manager and offered the available room at my original price, including breakfast. Before accepting, I confirmed that the rate would remain unchanged for all three nights and asked for the new arrangement in writing. The problem took fifteen minutes to resolve. Staying specific and focusing on a fair outcome was more effective than expressing general frustration.
lessons.passageTranslation: 我到达酒店时，前台找不到我的预订，尽管我有确认邮件。酒店几乎满房，唯一剩下的房间比我原订的更贵。我保持冷静，出示了预订编号、日期和付款记录。我说明自己理解错误可能发生，但不应该为并非由我造成的问题支付额外费用。前台与经理确认后，以原价提供了现有房间，并包含早餐。在接受之前，我确认三晚房价都会保持不变，并要求把新安排写下来。问题用了十五分钟解决。具体说明事实并专注于公平结果，比笼统表达不满更有效。

lessons.title: Disagreeing Without Creating Conflict
lessons.theme: 在日常或工作讨论中表达不同意见而不激化冲突
objectives: 先确认对方观点再表达异议
区分事实、担忧和个人偏好
把争论转向共同目标
warmUpQuestions: What makes a disagreement feel personal?
Which phrases help you disagree respectfully in English?
lessons.passage: Disagreement becomes difficult when people feel that their judgment or identity is being attacked. One useful approach is to separate the person from the proposal. Begin by identifying a point you genuinely understand, then state the specific part you see differently. Evidence helps, but it should be connected to a shared goal rather than used as a weapon. For example, instead of saying, 'Your plan is too risky,' you might say, 'I can see why speed matters. My concern is that we have not tested the payment process, and we both want the launch to be reliable.' This structure does not remove the disagreement. It makes the disagreement easier to examine. It also leaves room for a mixed solution, such as testing the highest-risk part first while allowing the rest of the work to continue.
lessons.passageTranslation: 当人们觉得自己的判断或身份受到攻击时，分歧就会变得棘手。一种有效的方法是把人和方案分开。先指出你真正理解的部分，再具体说明你在哪一点有不同看法。证据有帮助，但应与共同目标相连，而不是被当作武器。例如，不要说“你的方案风险太大”，可以说：“我明白速度为什么重要。我担心的是我们还没有测试付款流程，而我们都希望上线可靠。”这种结构不会消除分歧，却能让分歧更容易被讨论，也为混合方案留下空间，例如先测试风险最高的部分，同时让其他工作继续。

lessons.title: Negotiating a Realistic Deadline
lessons.theme: 在不破坏合作关系的前提下协商交期
objectives: 解释延期原因而不推卸责任
提出带条件的替代方案

warmUpQuestions: What usually causes delays in your work?
How do you say no to an unrealistic request without sounding negative?
lessons.passage: A customer asked us to deliver the entire order by Friday. At first, the deadline seemed impossible because one component would not arrive until Thursday afternoon. Instead of simply rejecting the request, I explained the constraint and separated the order into two batches. We could ship the urgent items on Friday and send the remainder the following Tuesday. I also offered daily progress updates so the customer would not be left uncertain. The customer accepted the proposal because it protected their most important launch date. The experience reminded me that a good negotiation is not about winning an argument. It is about identifying the other side's real priority and building a workable solution around it.
lessons.passageTranslation: 客户要求我们在星期五前交付全部订单。起初这个期限似乎不可能，因为其中一种零件要到星期四下午才能到货。我没有直接拒绝，而是说明限制，并把订单分成两批。紧急产品可以周五发出，其余部分下周二发出。我还提出每天汇报进度，避免客户因信息不足而不安。客户接受了方案，因为它保障了最重要的上市日期。这次经历让我意识到，好的谈判不是赢得争论，而是找出对方真正的优先事项，并围绕它建立可行方案。

lessons.title: Reading News Critically
lessons.theme: 识别报道中的事实、观点与缺失信息
objectives: 区分事实陈述与推断
指出报道缺少的证据
用谨慎语言表达判断
warmUpQuestions: What makes you trust a news story?
Have you ever shared information that later proved inaccurate?
lessons.passage: A convincing headline can create the impression that an issue has already been settled. However, responsible readers pause before accepting the conclusion. They ask who produced the information, what evidence is available, and whether alternative explanations were considered. Numbers can also mislead without being false. For example, a report may describe a fifty-percent increase but fail to mention that the number rose from two cases to three. Images are equally powerful because they can be genuine while still being presented without context. Critical reading does not mean assuming that every source is dishonest. It means matching the strength of our conclusion to the quality of the available evidence.
lessons.passageTranslation: 一个有说服力的标题会让人觉得问题已有定论。然而，负责任的读者在接受结论前会暂停思考：信息由谁发布，有什么证据，是否考虑了其他解释。数字即使真实也可能产生误导。例如，报道说增长了百分之五十，却没说明数字只是从两例增加到三例。图片也同样有力量，因为它可能真实，却脱离了语境。批判性阅读并不是认定所有来源都不诚实，而是让结论的确定程度与现有证据的质量相匹配。

vocabulary.definition: finally decided or no longer in doubt
vocabulary.example: The debate is far from settled.

vocabulary.definition: another possible reason for the same result
vocabulary.example: The article ignored several alternative explanations.

vocabulary.definition: without the background needed for correct understanding
vocabulary.example: The quotation is misleading without context.

vocabulary.definition: make the degree of certainty appropriate to the evidence
vocabulary.example: We should match the strength of our claim to the data.

quiz.explanation: The passage gives the example of an increase from two to three.

quiz.question: What does critical reading require?
quiz.explanation: The conclusion should be no stronger than the evidence supports.

lessons.title: Sustainable Choices at Work
lessons.theme: 讨论环保措施中的效果、成本与取舍
objectives: 比较环保方案的实际影响
讨论短期成本与长期收益
提出有依据的建议
warmUpQuestions: Which environmental action at work has the greatest impact?
When can a green choice create an unexpected cost?
lessons.passage: Companies often announce environmental targets, but the most visible action is not always the most effective one. Replacing plastic cups may improve public perception, yet changes in energy use, transport and product design can have a much larger impact. The difficulty is that these measures require investment and cooperation across departments. A realistic plan should therefore compare the full life cycle of each option rather than focusing on a single material. It should also measure progress in a way that employees and customers can understand. If a target is ambitious but impossible to verify, it may create more suspicion than trust. Sustainability becomes credible when an organization explains both what it has achieved and where it is still falling short.
lessons.passageTranslation: 公司经常宣布环保目标，但最显眼的行动不一定最有效。更换塑料杯可能改善公众印象，但能源使用、运输和产品设计的改变可能影响更大。困难在于这些措施需要投资和跨部门合作。因此，现实的计划应比较每个选择的完整生命周期，而不是只关注一种材料；还应以员工和客户能理解的方式衡量进展。如果目标雄心勃勃却无法验证，反而可能引起更多怀疑。一个组织既说明已取得的成果，也坦诚仍有不足，可持续发展才更可信。

lessons.title: Giving Constructive Feedback
lessons.theme: 在明确问题的同时保持尊重和可执行性
objectives: 描述具体行为而非评价人格
说明影响并提出下一步
回应不同意见
warmUpQuestions: What makes feedback difficult to accept?
Do you prefer direct or indirect feedback? Why?
lessons.passage: Feedback becomes useful when it is specific enough to guide action. Saying that a presentation was weak gives the speaker little direction. Explaining that the main recommendation appeared only at the end is more helpful because the problem can be corrected. Timing also matters. Immediate feedback can prevent repeated mistakes, but a tense public discussion may cause the recipient to become defensive. A private conversation after emotions have settled is often more productive. Finally, feedback should allow room for information we may not have. Asking what influenced a decision can reveal constraints that were invisible to us. Constructive feedback combines clarity with curiosity: it states the observed impact while remaining open to another perspective.
lessons.passageTranslation: 反馈要具体到能够指导行动，才真正有用。只说演示很差，演讲者不知道如何改进；说明主要建议直到最后才出现，则更有帮助，因为问题可以修正。时机也很重要。立即反馈能防止重复错误，但在紧张的公开讨论中可能让对方产生防御。等情绪平静后私下沟通往往更有效。最后，反馈应给未知信息留出空间。询问某个决定受什么因素影响，可能揭示我们看不到的限制。建设性反馈把清晰与好奇结合起来：既说明观察到的影响，也对另一种观点保持开放。

lessons.title: The Trade-offs of Hybrid Work
lessons.theme: 用平衡论证讨论远程与办公室协作
objectives: 构建包含让步的观点
比较效率与协作成本
总结复杂讨论
warmUpQuestions: Which tasks are easier at home?
What can remote teams lose besides face-to-face contact?
lessons.passage: Hybrid work is often discussed as a choice between freedom and control, but the real issue is coordination. Employees may concentrate better at home and avoid a long commute. At the same time, spontaneous questions become scheduled meetings, and new colleagues may struggle to learn informal practices. Requiring everyone to attend the office every day solves some coordination problems but removes much of the flexibility people value. A better policy defines which activities genuinely benefit from shared space. Teams might meet in person for planning, difficult decisions and relationship-building, while protecting remote time for focused individual work. The success of such a policy depends less on the number of office days than on whether expectations are clear and applied consistently.
lessons.passageTranslation: 混合办公常被描述为自由与控制之间的选择，但真正的问题是协调。员工在家可能更专注，也免去长途通勤；与此同时，临时提问变成预约会议，新同事也可能难以学到非正式的工作方式。要求所有人每天到办公室能解决部分协调问题，却会失去大家重视的灵活性。更好的政策应明确哪些活动真正受益于共享空间。团队可在线下进行规划、困难决策和关系建设，同时保留远程时间处理需要专注的个人工作。政策是否成功，与其说取决于到办公室几天，不如说取决于期望是否清晰并得到一致执行。

vocabulary.definition: happening naturally without advance planning
vocabulary.example: Remote work reduces spontaneous conversations.

vocabulary.definition: unwritten ways of doing work
vocabulary.example: New employees learn informal practices by observing colleagues.

lessons.title: Handling a Complex Complaint
lessons.theme: 承认影响、核实责任并恢复客户信任
objectives: 在事实未完全明确时承担沟通责任
提出调查和补救步骤
避免过度承诺
warmUpQuestions: What does an angry customer need first: facts, empathy or compensation?
Why can an immediate promise create a second problem?
lessons.passage: When a complaint is complex, the first response should not attempt to solve everything. Its purpose is to show that the problem has been understood and that a reliable process has begun. A useful response acknowledges the customer's experience, summarizes the issue and confirms when the next update will arrive. It should distinguish between what is already known and what still needs investigation. This prevents the company from making a promise it may later have to withdraw. Compensation may be appropriate, but offering it before understanding the cause can distract from the customer's real concern. Trust is usually restored through accurate updates and completed actions rather than through an impressive first message.
lessons.passageTranslation: 当投诉很复杂时，第一次回复不应试图解决所有问题，而应表明问题已被理解，并且可靠的处理流程已经启动。有效的回复会承认客户的经历，概括问题，并确认下次更新的时间；还应区分已知事实和仍需调查的内容，避免公司作出之后不得不撤回的承诺。赔偿可能合适，但在了解原因前提出赔偿，可能偏离客户真正关心的问题。恢复信任通常依靠准确的更新和落实的行动，而不是一封看起来很漂亮的首次回复。

lessons.title: Weekly Integration Challenge
lessons.theme: 整合本周语言：分析、协商、反馈与总结
objectives: 整合本周高频表达
连续表达观点两分钟
根据证据修正自己的结论
warmUpQuestions: Which lesson changed how you would communicate at work?
Which task was hardest: understanding, speaking or writing?
lessons.passage: Progress at B2 level is rarely about learning one more grammar rule. It is increasingly about control: choosing language that fits the purpose, recognizing uncertainty and connecting ideas clearly. A strong learner can explain a position, acknowledge a reasonable objection and still make a practical recommendation. This week’s topics may appear different, yet they share one skill. Whether we evaluate a headline, negotiate a deadline or answer a complaint, we must separate facts from assumptions and make our reasoning visible. Fluency matters, but reliable communication also requires revision. Recording an answer, noticing where the argument becomes vague and trying again is not a sign of failure. It is the process through which confident language becomes precise language.
lessons.passageTranslation: 到了 B2 水平，进步很少只是再学一条语法规则，而越来越在于控制力：选择符合目的的语言、识别不确定性并清晰连接观点。优秀的学习者能够解释立场，承认合理反对意见，同时仍提出可执行建议。本周主题看似不同，却共享一种能力：无论评估标题、协商期限还是回复投诉，我们都必须区分事实与假设，并让推理过程清晰可见。流利很重要，但可靠沟通也需要修订。录下回答、发现论证含糊之处再尝试一次，并不是失败，而是让自信表达变得精准的过程。

lessons.title: Clarifying a Change Request
lessons.theme: 在项目进行中澄清客户的新要求
objectives: 确认需求变化的具体范围
解释变化对时间和成本的影响
提出清晰的下一步安排
warmUpQuestions: What information do you need before accepting a change request?
How can you discuss extra cost without sounding unhelpful?
lessons.passage: Halfway through a packaging project, the customer asked us to replace the original material and add two new tests. The request sounded simple, but it affected several parts of the schedule. Before agreeing, I asked whether the new material was required for every model and which test standard the customer expected. I then summarized the change in writing and explained its likely impact on cost, sample approval and delivery. Rather than saying that the request was impossible, I offered two routes. We could keep the original launch date by changing only the priority models, or apply the change to the full order and move delivery by one week. The customer chose the first option. Clear questions prevented us from making an expensive assumption and gave both sides a shared basis for the decision.
lessons.passageTranslation: 包装项目进行到一半时，客户要求更换原材料并增加两项测试。这个要求听起来简单，却会影响进度的多个环节。在答应之前，我先确认新材料是否适用于所有型号，以及客户要求哪一种测试标准。随后我用书面方式总结变更，并说明它可能对成本、样品批准和交付造成的影响。我没有直接说要求无法实现，而是提供两条路径：如果只更改优先型号，可以保留原上市日期；如果整批订单都变更，交付则需要延后一周。客户选择了第一种。清晰的问题避免了代价高昂的假设，也为双方决策建立了共同依据。
